$comment: StoryRail for the office squad. Set once for the whole squad and commit; a developer only needs a GitLab token. The applications of a story come from its "## Applications" section in GitLab, not from this file. `node scripts/storyrail-workspace.mjs todo` lists what is still to fill in. See docs/storyrail/SETUP.md.

gitlab.$comment: Your GitLab. Agents reach it with a personal access token (scope api) through scripts/storyrail-gitlab.mjs, or through the GitLab MCP server if it is configured in Bob. Never put the token in this file.
gitlab.group: TODO(office): the GitLab group your applications live in, e.g. insu

backlog.$comment: The GitLab project where the user stories and bugs live (with the Screen and API documents attached). Issue numbers are this project's issue IIDs.

hub.$comment: This repo (agents, dashboard, run records) on your GitLab.

apps.$comment: Applications are found by name in gitlab.group (INSU-ta01 → a project called INSU-ta01 or INSU-ta01-…), and frontend or backend is read from the repo. Only add an entry to map when a name doesn't match its project, e.g. "INSU-ta01": "insu/task-api", or { "project": "insu/x", "type": "backend" }.

appTypes.$comment: How each kind of application is built and tested. The same for every app of that kind; an app's own README or package.json scripts win when they say otherwise.

frontend.verify: npm ci && npm run lint && npm run typecheck --if-present && npm test && npm run build

backend.stub: WireMock (or the stub tool the app's tests already use), fed from the provider's contract

mergeRequests.$comment: Step 7: one MR per application in the run, merged in dependency order (providers first, from the story's Applications section). waitForMrPipeline: wait for the MR pipeline before asking you to merge.

build.$comment: Step 2. parallel: build every application at the same time, each against the contracts of the apps it calls (stubbed in its tests). sequential: build them one after the other, providers first.

scans.$comment: Quality scans in steps 4 and 6, per kind of application. mode: local = run the command on your machine before anything is pushed; ci = push the branch, let its GitLab pipeline run the scan job, then read the result; off = skip. Commands run from the app's folder; $APP is the application name, $BRANCH the run branch. Tokens come from environment variables, never from this file.

sonar.gate: Quality gate passed and no open blocker or critical issue on new code

commands.backend: TODO(office): e.g. sourceanalyzer -b $APP -clean && sourceanalyzer -b $APP mvn -B -q package -DskipTests && sourceanalyzer -b $APP -scan -f target/fortify.fpr

fortify.results: TODO(office): e.g. FPRUtility -information -search -query "[fortify priority order]:critical OR [fortify priority order]:high" -project target/fortify.fpr

commands.backend: TODO(office): e.g. java -jar $NEXUS_IQ_CLI -s $NEXUS_IQ_URL -a $NEXUS_IQ_USER:$NEXUS_IQ_TOKEN -i $APP -t build -r nexus-iq.json target/

nexusIQ.gate: No policy violation at Critical or Severe

designSystem.$comment: The company component library the frontend must build screens from. Set enabled to true once the TODO(office) values are filled in; the rules in .bob/rules-sr-fe-dev/02-design-system.md then apply.
designSystem.package: TODO(office): npm package of the component library, e.g. @your-org/ui-components
designSystem.storybookUrl: TODO(office): URL of the Storybook that documents it

references.$comment: Existing applications the developers copy patterns from. Cloned read-only into references/ by `node scripts/storyrail-workspace.mjs sync`; no mode may edit them. Keep them on your internal GitLab, never in a public repo.

squad.$comment: The squad as shown on the dashboard. stations = the status ids each member reports on; dev@frontend / dev@backend etc. mean that step for every frontend / backend application of the run. brief = the mode's rule folder (sr-*) or 'orchestrator'; outOfScope = a person who works outside StoryRail.
